clue.text: Railway expert allowed to form a band

blocks.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway
an ace is someone highly skilled
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A railway specialist is permitted to start up a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians, but it is a ring worn on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental ring or strip worn around the wrist, which is one kind of band.

clue.text: Remain on hold, and mind your manners!

blocks.note: to be is to exist or remain
to have is to hold or possess

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay on the line while being polite, like a switchboard order.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means one piece sits above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to behave is an order to act politely, the same command as mind your manners.

clue.text: Welsh lake rising over flower of translucent whiteness

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the lake's name is reversed

blocks.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A Welsh lake rises above a pale, glowing flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white stone that lets some light through, so as an adjective it means pure translucent white.

clue.text: Directions so accepted make us show eagerness

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so the directions hold the other word inside

blocks.note: ENE is east-north-east, a compass point combining directions
thus means so, in this way

explanation.surface: Instructions being taken on board make us keen.
explanation.walkthrough: ENE stands for east-north-east, so one compass point supplies three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to express excited interest, so it means showing eagerness or zeal.

clue.text: Sort of bird to repent going topless!

indicators.note: losing the top of a down word means its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: to regret something is to repent of it

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a bird that will be sorry for going topless.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird of marshes and shallow water.

clue.text: Conditional backing by a second firm results in failure

indicators.note: something backing goes in reverse, so the conditional word is read from right to left

blocks.note: if introduces a condition
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
Co. is short for company

explanation.surface: A deal that depends on conditions, propped up by a second company, ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as an adjective meaning solid, but it is a company, abbreviated CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete and ludicrous flop, so it is an outright failure.

clue.text: Fashionable woman with sex appeal has to succeed

blocks.note: in means in fashion
her is a pronoun for a woman
it is an old word for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A stylish, attractive woman is bound to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' looks like do well, but it means follow on, as an heir does.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to take their place after them, and to inherit is to receive their title or property.

clue.text: Nurse holding raise up to scorn

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word for raise is reversed
something holding another clasps it inside, so the nurse wraps round the rest

blocks.note: SRN is State Registered Nurse, a former British nursing qualification
to raise something is to put it up

explanation.surface: A nurse lifts someone up to treat them with contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: SRN was the title of a fully qualified nurse in Britain until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with disdain, the same as treating something with scorn.

clue.text: Speculator looking after connections in the exchange?

definitions.text: looking after connections in the exchange?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dealer who trades shares for profit

blocks.clueFragment: looking after connections in the exchange?
blocks.note: second meaning: the person at a telephone exchange who puts calls through

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' first suggests the stock exchange, matching the speculator; the question mark signals the telephone exchange instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A market dealer is called a shrewd operator, and a switchboard worker connecting telephone calls is also known by this title.

clue.text: Language of a holy man seen about in Sark, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the words could be arranged otherwise, so the letters are rearranged
something seen about another wraps around it, so the holy man goes outside the rest

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint turns up on Sark speaking a strange tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small island in the Channel Islands. The rearranged letters go between the S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical tongue of India, used in Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Drama of Shaw's brief holiday in home by river

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the holiday goes within the home

blocks.note: the hearth is the fireside, used to mean home
a short holiday is a break
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A short holiday at home beside a river, offered as a description of a Shaw play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak House is a play by George Bernard Shaw, first staged in 1920.

clue.text: Road or rail carrier offers through passage

blocks.note: via means by way of, through
a duct is a channel or passage

explanation.surface: A transport route is described as giving a way across.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge on arches that carries a road or railway over a valley.

clue.text: Lilac is no good in an Asian republic

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside, so the no-good letters go within the country

blocks.note: Syria is a republic in western Asia
NG is the usual abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub is said to do badly in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus name for the lilac shrubs, and gardeners use it as their common name too.

clue.text: Flag for vessel crossing river

indicators.note: a ship crossing a river has the river across its middle, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a steamer is a steamship
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A pennant flown by a ship as it crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast, a kind of flag.

clue.text: Unite, say, with the enemy living near the sea

indicators.note: say asks for words as spoken, so the result matches how they sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: to marry is to unite
time is the enemy, as in the old saying

explanation.surface: Joining forces with the foe while staying near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, the answer sounds like marry time; 'time, the enemy' is a set phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means connected with or bordering the sea, so a maritime people live along the coast.

clue.text: In Scotland, a drink originally offered to a poet

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: tass is a Scots word for a cup or a small drink
the opening letter of offered

explanation.surface: North of the border, someone hands a dram to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Scotland' marks TASS as Scottish dialect for a cup or a dram.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the sixteenth-century Italian author of the epic Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Alarming, when a bird swallows half of it!

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is just one letter, so only part of the word is kept
what is swallowed ends up inside, so the bird takes the letter into its middle

blocks.note: the starling is a common speckled songbird
the second half of it

explanation.surface: It is shocking to watch a bird gulp down half of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling gives a sudden shock or surprise, which makes it alarming.

clue.text: Worn out mine upholds the law almost to the end

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the law is dropped

blocks.note: a decree is an order with the force of law
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: An exhausted colliery that keeps to the law right up to its closure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the mine upholds, or sits under, the shortened law.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes something old and in poor condition, weakened by age and use, so worn out.

clue.text: Spooky Eastern Lake

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A haunted-sounding lake somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is strange and frightening in a ghostly, unsettling way.

clue.text: Omission in pronouncement made by priest on mountain

blocks.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A slip in a statement delivered by a priest on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the priest above the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the dropping of a sound or syllable in speech, as in can't for cannot.

clue.text: Clubman freely ran riot around centre of Newcastle

indicators.note: doing something freely means without fixed order, so these letters are rearranged at will
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the fifth of nine letters, the middle one

explanation.surface: A member of a club went on the rampage in the middle of Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubman' suggests a night-club reveller, fitting the riot, but it means a member of a service club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotarian belongs to Rotary International, a worldwide service club for business and professional people.

clue.text: Search in anger when posh decoration is hidden

indicators.note: what is hidden is tucked away inside something else, here inside the anger

blocks.note: rage is violent anger
U means upper-class, a label coined for posh usage
MM is the Military Medal, a British award

explanation.surface: Someone hunts about angrily because a smart medal has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: UMM goes between the R and AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search untidily through things, turning them over while looking for something.

clue.text: Bishop managed church office, though not the main one

definitions.text: office, though not the main one

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run something is to manage it
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bishop ran a church office that was not headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local outlet of a bank or business, a subsidiary site rather than head office.

clue.text: A traveller isn't commonly employed to improve the decoration

blocks.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman is not usually hired to smarten up a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaint a room is to give it a fresh coat of colour, renewing and improving its decor.

clue.text: Fish for Bess's man?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sea bream of American waters
second meaning: the hero of Gershwin's opera, who loves Bess

explanation.definitionFit: The porgy is a food fish of the sea bream family, and Porgy and Bess is the Gershwin opera.

clue.text: Team leader in a bad mood? The devil he is!

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
being in something means sitting inside it, so the leading letter goes within the mood

blocks.note: a temper is a fit of anger
the opening letter of team

explanation.surface: The captain of a side is in a foul mood, and someone remarks what a devil he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team leader' looks like a captain, but it only asks for a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition Satan is called the Tempter, the one who lures people into sin.

clue.text: The principle of evicting people from-a rented flat?

indicators.note: evicting throws occupants out, so those letters are removed from the dwelling

blocks.note: a tenement is a building of rented flats, or one such flat
men are people

explanation.surface: A wry question about the rule behind turfing tenants out of a let.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing MEN from the middle of TENEMENT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a guiding principle.

clue.text: Possibly Fairfax's main part in a real disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and out of place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Fairfax's leading role is in a real catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Fairfax commanded the Parliamentary army against the King in the English Civil War; 'possibly' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairfax fought for Parliament against Charles I, so he is an example of a supporter of that side in the Civil War.

clue.text: Making an effort like the 1st Baron Jeffreys

blocks.note: first meaning: attempting, having a go
second meaning: hearing cases in court, as the notorious hanging judge did

explanation.walkthrough: George Jeffreys, 1st Baron Jeffreys, was the judge of the Bloody Assizes of 1685, infamous for his harsh sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means attempting, and also conducting a court case, which is what a judge such as Jeffreys does.

clue.text: Full complement of vigour

blocks.note: first meaning: the total number of people in a unit
second meaning: power and energy

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the full number of members on a roll, as in a regiment, and physical force or power.
